title: Phenomenology of reactive and dissipative nutation in antiferromagnets
authors: Erlend Syljuåsen, Hans Gløckner Giil, Arne Brataas
abstract: We formulate equations of motion for uniform magnetization dynamics in multisublattice magnets, with emphasis on a recently proposed inertial damping torque. We include intra- and intersublattice contributions to Gilbert damping, reactive inertia, and inertial damping. For a two-sublattice uniaxial antiferromagnet in an easy-axis static magnetic field, we derive the dynamical magnetic susceptibilities and approximate eigenfrequencies across all field-dependent equilibrium phases. In particular, we show how inertial damping affects the relaxation of the nutational modes and propose an experimental protocol to determine the dynamical coefficients.
summary: This theoretical work develops an advanced model for magnetization dynamics in antiferromagnets by incorporating inertial damping alongside standard damping mechanisms. By analyzing the system across three magnetic phases, the authors derive the full spectrum of eigenfrequencies and propose an experimental protocol to measure the underlying dynamical coefficients.
main_problem: The paper formulates and analyzes the equations of motion for uniform magnetization dynamics in multisublattice magnets, focusing on the inclusion of reactive inertia and a novel inertial damping torque.
main_result: The model successfully derives the dynamical magnetic susceptibilities and eigenfrequencies across three distinct magnetic phases (AP, CA, FP), showing how inertial damping affects the relaxation of nutational modes.
method: The methodology involves deriving phenomenological equations of motion, linearizing them around equilibrium points, and calculating the eigenfrequencies by solving the determinant of the resulting dynamical matrix.
model_or_system: The system is a general multisublattice magnet, specifically applied to a two-sublattice uniaxial antiferromagnet. Dynamics are described using Néel ($\mathbf{n}$) and magnetization ($\mathbf{m}$) vectors, constrained by fixed-length conditions.
key_observables: Dynamical magnetic susceptibilities ($\chi$), resonance frequencies ($\Omega = \omega - i\Gamma$), and linewidths of precessional and nutational modes.
important_parameters: Exchange frequency ($\omega_E$), anisotropy frequency ($\omega_A$), Zeeman frequency ($\omega_H$), and various damping coefficients (Gilbert, inertial, etc.).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes fixed magnitudes for magnetization vectors and relies on perturbative expansions in damping parameters, particularly in the exchange-dominated regime.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the field dependence of eigenfrequencies and quality factors across the AP, CA, and FP phases, summarizing the results in Table I.
paper_structure: The paper builds from general equations of motion for multisublattice magnets to specific derivations for the two-sublattice case. It analyzes linear response around three equilibrium phases (AP, CA, FP) by calculating dynamical susceptibilities and solving for eigenfrequencies in different approximations.
why_interesting: The detailed treatment of inertial damping and the derivation of an 'inertial Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert equation' provides a sophisticated framework for modeling high-frequency dynamics in magnetic materials, relevant to understanding quantum coherence in spin systems.
